top_reviews.title: Love Oboz and Love These Boots!
top_reviews.text: I had never heard of Oboz before until I ordered a pair of boots in a different style a few years ago.  I fell in love with this brand and when I saw this style, which looked like it had a bit more ankle support, I just had to order them.  Straight out of the box, I couldn't believe how light they were.  Even with thick socks, they were easy to pull on.  I usually wear a size 7 in a shoe, but I ordered a 8.5 in these boots because they seem to run just a little bit small and my toe kept hitting the front of the boot. I knew I needed a larger size in addition to the toe thing because my feet swell when out hiking. The 8.5 fits wonderfully and allows me room to wear thick hiking socks with a little bit of wiggle room, but snug enough to not have a loose heel.  I've worn these boots out in the field on a number of different occasions and have not had a single blister or hot spot.  Plus, they have good ankle support for me and the tread is sturdy and has kept me me from slipping in wet or slick situations.  I also really like the bright red color I ordered.  I did, however, have to replace the rounded laces with flat laces in order to keep the laces from coming untied.  I have this issue with pretty much all of my hiking boots and really wish hiking boots would  come with flat laces in general.  Once I replaced the round laces with flat ones, I had no more problems.  As for arch support - I have flat feet so I can't really tell you much about that, except that my feet are  comfortable and the boots are not heavy and clunky like others I have in my closet.  I know how quickly styles come and go, and I like this particular style so much, I ordered another pair just to have after this pair wears out.

top_reviews.title: First pair of Oboz
top_reviews.text: I tried these boots on at the local outfitters.  Loved them but couldn't bring myself to spend the asking price of $160.  The lady at the outfitter said her and her daughter wear them often and have done many hikes.  They like these boots//shoes so much that they carry a great selection.  She did recommend getting a half size larger to allow the extra room in toe area for up and down trails, otherwise you would end up with sore toes.... which is exactly what was happing with my current pair of hikers. She also mentioned to tie them a little loose around the ankle until they are broken in.  I ordered these about a month ago. Second day I had them I went to appalachian trail for two mile waterfall hike. I purposely stepped in water at the falls and NO wet feet!  I walk 2-13 miles a day and have had no sores or rubbing.  They wear well and I have found now that they are my go to boot!  Getting a pair for my husband!

top_reviews.title: Best Hiking Boots
top_reviews.text: I LOVE these hiking boots.  I hike/trail walk 6+ miles a day and from day 1 with these boots they have been extremely comfortable (and I have plantar fasciitis so thats saying something).  I recently bought Anuh because they were lighter in weight but they are stiff and the insoles are not very comfortable.  This is my second pair of Oboz Women's Bridger B-DRY Hiking Boot and I will continue to buy them.  My first pair lasted 3+ years and although the boots still look and feel great they are no longer waterproof so I needed to replace them.

top_reviews.title: Comfortable, Stylish, Durable but Expensive. Worth it?
top_reviews.text:
So let's get right to the crux of this flip flop. The price.
Is it worth it?
That's really up to you, the specifics of your body & what you want out of them.

FYI, this is a 1 year review & I wear these EVERY day for at least several hours.
Sometimes all day but not all day every day.
*apologies for how dirty they are in the photos*

The Good:
• Very comfortable to me & my size 12/13 wide feet
• 100% leather touches your skin, it feels great... to me
• Supportive enough but not overly so. This is very important to me as I wear flip-flops to allow my feet to move freely as compared to boots or shoes
• Very Durable for what I use & wanted them for. Which is mostly as: house shoes, walking around town, shopping, beaches, & light trails - very light; minimal elevation changes & well kept. At 1 year of everyday use you can see that there is very little wear on the leather or the treads
• Super Stylish - love the way these look! I mean just look at the details in the leather, the stitching, even the treads. Just beautiful

The Bad:
• Expensive!!! The most expensive flip-flops I own BY FAR.
That said, I certainly have/ have had sandals that are right up there & they haven't lasted & weren't nearly as comfy
• Inconsistent / Quality Control Issues:
▪︎This is my 2nd set of these. To be fair, maybe they just run big as my nominal size is 12.5 wide so I normally go for 13s when companies don't offer 12.5s but the 13s of these were HUGE. Didn't fit at all. Again, this may not be a fault of the company or the flip-flop
▪︎ Inconsistency between each flip-flop. As you can see in the pictures. My left flip-flop has much more pronounced/deeper etching in the leather, which I prefer for visual & functional (more on that later) reasons
• NOT for water use - going back to those etchings in the leather. The right flip-flop has no grip at all on your foot while it's wet. Very slippery. Even the deeper etched left flip-flop has very poor foot traction when wet. Also, I'd strongly warn against using these for water anyway because you risk damaging the leather unless you're very careful about not soaking them too long, drying them, & then treating the leather. Actually the only damage/ wear these have is from water damage. The right flip-flop's leather has cracked right behind the ball of my foot but it's still very serviceable.

Conclusion:
These are a very well made, beautiful, comfortable & durable flip-flop depending on your intended use for them.

These are best suited for: walking around your house, on well maintained terrain, & for strolling the sands on the beaches but you should kick them off before getting to the waterline.

These things are EXPENSIVE & they aren't made for hard work or tough terrain so keep that in mind.

I'll try to update if anything changes or at the 2yr mark. Whichever happens first.

Hope this helps someone decide.
Take care everyone. 🙂

top_reviews.title: STOP IT! Good sandals aren't cheap, and cheap sandals aren't good-- period.
top_reviews.text:
Gotta laugh at the 1-star reviews & the crying like little girls - pffft. Here's my pair, worn DAILY for +/- 11 months and worn 99% of the time on concrete, gravel, and other hard surfaces, and I weigh 185. Again, DAILY. So sorry about your little boo-boo's (like, that's the manufacturers' fault?!), and how they're slippery when wet (imagine: common sense... ), and how they 'fell apart' -- stop it. Try HARD to be a man and stop crying like a little girl 'cause it's embarrassing to another man.

I've purchased 8 pairs over the past 8 years and will continue to do so. I so wish they were NOT commie made, however, I am here to endorse the quality; I would NOT buy something a second time if it were garbage. As I'm about to purchase another pair as I do every year about this time, I had to chime in for the ridiculous 1-stars. Moreover, as a design engineer who apprieciates quality and tries very hard to avoid low-quality products, I trust you won't be disappointed unless of course, you are a crybaby.

Cheers
Robert Kuchta

top_reviews.title: Love Oboz and Love These Boots!
top_reviews.text: I had never heard of Oboz before until I ordered a pair of boots in a different style a few years ago.  I fell in love with this brand and when I saw this style, which looked like it had a bit more ankle support, I just had to order them.  Straight out of the box, I couldn't believe how light they were.  Even with thick socks, they were easy to pull on.  I usually wear a size 7 in a shoe, but I ordered a 8.5 in these boots because they seem to run just a little bit small and my toe kept hitting the front of the boot. I knew I needed a larger size in addition to the toe thing because my feet swell when out hiking. The 8.5 fits wonderfully and allows me room to wear thick hiking socks with a little bit of wiggle room, but snug enough to not have a loose heel.  I've worn these boots out in the field on a number of different occasions and have not had a single blister or hot spot.  Plus, they have good ankle support for me and the tread is sturdy and has kept me me from slipping in wet or slick situations.  I also really like the bright red color I ordered.  I did, however, have to replace the rounded laces with flat laces in order to keep the laces from coming untied.  I have this issue with pretty much all of my hiking boots and really wish hiking boots would  come with flat laces in general.  Once I replaced the round laces with flat ones, I had no more problems.  As for arch support - I have flat feet so I can't really tell you much about that, except that my feet are  comfortable and the boots are not heavy and clunky like others I have in my closet.  I know how quickly styles come and go, and I like this particular style so much, I ordered another pair just to have after this pair wears out.

top_reviews.title: First pair of Oboz
top_reviews.text: I tried these boots on at the local outfitters.  Loved them but couldn't bring myself to spend the asking price of $160.  The lady at the outfitter said her and her daughter wear them often and have done many hikes.  They like these boots//shoes so much that they carry a great selection.  She did recommend getting a half size larger to allow the extra room in toe area for up and down trails, otherwise you would end up with sore toes.... which is exactly what was happing with my current pair of hikers. She also mentioned to tie them a little loose around the ankle until they are broken in.  I ordered these about a month ago. Second day I had them I went to appalachian trail for two mile waterfall hike. I purposely stepped in water at the falls and NO wet feet!  I walk 2-13 miles a day and have had no sores or rubbing.  They wear well and I have found now that they are my go to boot!  Getting a pair for my husband!

top_reviews.title: Best Hiking Boots
top_reviews.text: I LOVE these hiking boots.  I hike/trail walk 6+ miles a day and from day 1 with these boots they have been extremely comfortable (and I have plantar fasciitis so thats saying something).  I recently bought Anuh because they were lighter in weight but they are stiff and the insoles are not very comfortable.  This is my second pair of Oboz Women's Bridger B-DRY Hiking Boot and I will continue to buy them.  My first pair lasted 3+ years and although the boots still look and feel great they are no longer waterproof so I needed to replace them.

top_reviews.title: Comfortable, Stylish, Durable but Expensive. Worth it?
top_reviews.text:
So let's get right to the crux of this flip flop. The price.
Is it worth it?
That's really up to you, the specifics of your body & what you want out of them.

FYI, this is a 1 year review & I wear these EVERY day for at least several hours.
Sometimes all day but not all day every day.
*apologies for how dirty they are in the photos*

The Good:
• Very comfortable to me & my size 12/13 wide feet
• 100% leather touches your skin, it feels great... to me
• Supportive enough but not overly so. This is very important to me as I wear flip-flops to allow my feet to move freely as compared to boots or shoes
• Very Durable for what I use & wanted them for. Which is mostly as: house shoes, walking around town, shopping, beaches, & light trails - very light; minimal elevation changes & well kept. At 1 year of everyday use you can see that there is very little wear on the leather or the treads
• Super Stylish - love the way these look! I mean just look at the details in the leather, the stitching, even the treads. Just beautiful

The Bad:
• Expensive!!! The most expensive flip-flops I own BY FAR.
That said, I certainly have/ have had sandals that are right up there & they haven't lasted & weren't nearly as comfy
• Inconsistent / Quality Control Issues:
▪︎This is my 2nd set of these. To be fair, maybe they just run big as my nominal size is 12.5 wide so I normally go for 13s when companies don't offer 12.5s but the 13s of these were HUGE. Didn't fit at all. Again, this may not be a fault of the company or the flip-flop
▪︎ Inconsistency between each flip-flop. As you can see in the pictures. My left flip-flop has much more pronounced/deeper etching in the leather, which I prefer for visual & functional (more on that later) reasons
• NOT for water use - going back to those etchings in the leather. The right flip-flop has no grip at all on your foot while it's wet. Very slippery. Even the deeper etched left flip-flop has very poor foot traction when wet. Also, I'd strongly warn against using these for water anyway because you risk damaging the leather unless you're very careful about not soaking them too long, drying them, & then treating the leather. Actually the only damage/ wear these have is from water damage. The right flip-flop's leather has cracked right behind the ball of my foot but it's still very serviceable.

Conclusion:
These are a very well made, beautiful, comfortable & durable flip-flop depending on your intended use for them.

These are best suited for: walking around your house, on well maintained terrain, & for strolling the sands on the beaches but you should kick them off before getting to the waterline.

These things are EXPENSIVE & they aren't made for hard work or tough terrain so keep that in mind.

I'll try to update if anything changes or at the 2yr mark. Whichever happens first.

Hope this helps someone decide.
Take care everyone. 🙂

top_reviews.title: STOP IT! Good sandals aren't cheap, and cheap sandals aren't good-- period.
top_reviews.text:
Gotta laugh at the 1-star reviews & the crying like little girls - pffft. Here's my pair, worn DAILY for +/- 11 months and worn 99% of the time on concrete, gravel, and other hard surfaces, and I weigh 185. Again, DAILY. So sorry about your little boo-boo's (like, that's the manufacturers' fault?!), and how they're slippery when wet (imagine: common sense... ), and how they 'fell apart' -- stop it. Try HARD to be a man and stop crying like a little girl 'cause it's embarrassing to another man.

I've purchased 8 pairs over the past 8 years and will continue to do so. I so wish they were NOT commie made, however, I am here to endorse the quality; I would NOT buy something a second time if it were garbage. As I'm about to purchase another pair as I do every year about this time, I had to chime in for the ridiculous 1-stars. Moreover, as a design engineer who apprieciates quality and tries very hard to avoid low-quality products, I trust you won't be disappointed unless of course, you are a crybaby.

Cheers
Robert Kuchta
